question: True or false: across many studies, people in better-paid jobs are much more satisfied with their work?
answer: False. Judge and colleagues pooled studies of thousands of employees and found the correlation between pay level and job satisfaction was about 0.15: pay accounted for roughly 2% of the differences in how much people liked their jobs. A well-paid job and a satisfying job were close to separate questions.
move: Ask what you will do all day, not only what it pays.
ask: If my pay stayed the same, which parts of my work would I keep and which would I change?
trap: Pay seems the main thing a job gives, so it should drive liking.
source: Judge and colleagues, J. Vocational Behavior, 2010
reference: Judge, Piccolo, Podsakoff, Shaw and Rich, The relationship between pay and job satisfaction: A meta-analysis of the literature, Journal of Vocational Behavior, 2010
